OK guys I found a fix! 

In my case there was a leftover/old `tui.json` file in `~/.config/opencode/`. 

Removing or renaming the file fixes it.

Example command:
`mv ~/.config/opencode/tui.json ~/.config/opencode/tui.backup.json` 

I've personally never touched `tui.json`, at least not to my knowledge. So I think it's a leftover file from older versions which wasn't removed during the update process.

OS:
Windows 11

OpenCode version:
v1.15.5

Model:
MiniMax M2.5

Steps to reproduce:

1. Open OpenCode Desktop v1.15.5
2. Start a new session in Build mode
3. Use MiniMax M2.5 as the model
4. Send very small prompts such as:

   * “hi”
   * “banana”
   * “reply only with banana”
5. Continue chatting for a few messages

Observed behavior:
The assistant first responds normally, but then the session sometimes becomes compacted and the chat shows structured task-summary sections such as:

* Goal
* Constraints & Preferences
* Progress
* Next Steps
* Critical Context

Sometimes “Session compacted” also appears in the timeline.

After compaction, MiniMax may continue replying in this structured task-summary style even for casual prompts.

Expected behavior:
Casual prompts should continue producing normal conversational responses after compaction instead of switching into persistent task-summary formatting.

Notes:
This behavior appears much more frequently with MiniMax M2.5 than with Claude/GPT models in the same environment.

- delegation mode requested
- delegation mode actually available

Based on my search, I found a potentially related PR:

**PR #28126** - `fix(opencode): order messages by (time.created, id) at runLoop exit`
https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/28126

This PR appears to address message ordering in the session prompt loop, which is closely related to the current PR's focus on fixing prompt queue ordering when prompts are submitted while a session is running. Both PRs deal with message ordering and turn sequence in the prompt loop execution.

Great fix for the pending/running/error states! 

One gap: the **completed** `tool_call_update` handler still uses `title: part.state.title` directly (lines ~387 and ~871 in `agent.ts`). For MCP and plugin-registered tools (like ADV) that don`t set a custom `state.title`, this sends `""` — causing ACP clients like Zed to show blank hammer rows.

Your `toolTitle` helper needs one tweak to handle this: change the truthiness check so empty string `""` falls through to `part.tool`:

```ts
// Current — completed title returns "" for empty titles
if ("title" in part.state \&\& typeof part.state.title === "string") return part.state.title

// Fixed — empty string falls through to part.tool
if ("title" in part.state \&\& part.state.title) return part.state.title
```

Then apply `this.toolTitle(part)` to the two completed handlers (same pattern as the running/error handlers). Verified this works on v1.15.5 — the only change needed was `title: part.state.title || part.tool` at both completed sites.

Happy to open a follow-up PR if that is easier.

The real issue is tmux `allow-passthrough off` default blocking DCS forwarding. Workaround: `set -g allow-passthrough on` in tmux.conf, or `env -u TMUX opencode` to use bare OSC 52 (needs `set-clipboard on`).
